Waze Starts Showing Raised Crossing Notifications on Android Auto and CarPlay
8 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
Waze has started showing notifications for incoming raised crossings, therefore giving drivers more time to slow down.
While the ability to add raised crossings to Waze has been around since at least July for map editors, the notifications have now started to appear for drivers in Europe. Considering these are considered permanent road features, which map editors must manually add to the map based on their location, users won’t be able to report them through the hazard reporting button.
If the raised crossings don’t show up for you just yet, the best option is to reach out to your local Waze map editor community and wait for the maps to be updated.
Prior to this update, the raised crossings were marked on the map as a speed bump. The introduction of this update makes more sense, as the raised crossings also allow pedestrians to cross the street and also double as a speed bump.
The introduction of raised crossing notifications is not tied to a specific app version, as the alerts are pushed through a server-side update. However, you should still update to the latest version to get the most recent bug fixes and improvements. I am using the most recent Waze version published on the App Store on an iPhone 15 Pro and CarPlay, but the raised crossings also appear on my wife’s iPhone 17 that runs an older version of Waze.
Meanwhile, the addition of this feature also serves as another reminder that Google still doesn’t plan to merge Google Maps and Waze. The reason is as simple as it can be: while Google Maps remains an all-in-one mapping platform that focuses on the essential capabilities and only gets the common traffic hazards, Waze keeps expanding into new directions with support for more traffic reports.
For example, while Waze can warn of speed bumps and raised crossings, Google Maps only shows user-reported hazards, such as accidents and roadworks. Google Maps also imports police reports from Waze, but otherwise, the application doesn’t support permanent road features similar to those currently available in Waze.
The raised crossing alerts are live on all platforms where Waze is available, including not only mobile devices, but also Android Auto and CarPlay. This makes sense, considering the experience on Android Auto and CarPlay is still powered by a smartphone. You’ll see an alert on the screen when you approach a pinned raised crossing - you can also disable these notifications separately, as they are part of the permanent road features group.
If you want to disable all permanent road features in Waze, including raised crossings and speed bumps, you must open the app, tap the icon to open the side menu, and head over to Settings > Map Display > Reports, and look for the one that you want to block from showing up on the screen.
